test_cases.description: Constructor returns a non-nil *GitRunner and nil error when host git version is >= 2.38 and workDir exists.
preconditions: Host has git >= 2.38 installed and on PATH
A valid temporary directory exists on the filesystem
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, err := New(tmpDir, nil); assert err == nil; assert runner != nil

test_cases.description: Constructor returns (nil, error) with a message identifying the detected version and the 2.38 minimum when git version is below 2.38.
preconditions: A fake git binary on PATH that outputs 'git version 2.37.0' is available, OR the test is skipped if host git is >= 2.38 and no fake binary can be injected
A valid temporary directory exists
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, err := New(tmpDir, nil); assert runner == nil; assert err != nil; assert errorMessage(err) contains '2.37'; assert errorMessage(err) contains '2.38'

test_cases.description: Constructor returns (nil, error) wrapping the exec failure when git is not found on PATH.
preconditions: PATH is set to a directory that does not contain a git binary
A valid temporary directory exists

expected.err: non-nil error describing exec failure (e.g., 'executable file not found in $PATH')

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, err := New(tmpDir, nil); assert runner == nil; assert err != nil; assert errorMessage(err) contains 'exec' or 'not found'

test_cases.description: Constructor accepts any valid directory path as workDir, including a non-git-repository directory such as os.TempDir().
preconditions: Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH
os.TempDir() exists and is not a git repository
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, err := New(os.TempDir(), nil); assert err == nil; assert runner != nil

test_cases.description: Every git subprocess spawned by GitRunner has GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 in its environment.
preconditions: A *GitRunner is constructed with a valid workDir and nil extraEnv
Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH

expected.env: subprocess environment contains GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, _ := New(tmpDir, nil); out, err := runner.Run(ctx, 'env'); assert err == nil; assert out contains 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh'; assert out contains 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0'; assert out contains 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1'

test_cases.description: Safety variables are appended after extraEnv so they unconditionally take precedence over any conflicting caller-supplied values.
preconditions: A *GitRunner is constructed with extraEnv containing GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=git:http
Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH

expected.env: subprocess environment's last occurrence of GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL is file:https:ssh

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, _ := New(tmpDir, []string{'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=git:http'}); out, _ := runner.Run(ctx, 'env'); lines := splitLines(out); lastGAP := lastOccurrence(lines, 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL='); assert lastGAP == 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh'

test_cases.description: When a caller passes a different GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL in extraEnv, the hardcoded file:https:ssh value wins because it is appended last.
preconditions: A *GitRunner is constructed with extraEnv containing GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https
Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH

expected.env: effective GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL in subprocess is file:https:ssh, not https

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, _ := New(tmpDir, []string{'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https'}); out, _ := runner.Run(ctx, 'env'); assert lastOccurrence(out, 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=') == 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh'

test_cases.description: Run returns trimmed stdout and nil error when the git subprocess exits with code 0.
preconditions: A *GitRunner is constructed with a valid git repository as workDir
Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, _ := New(repoDir, nil); out, err := runner.Run(ctx, 'rev-parse', '--git-dir'); assert err == nil; assert strings.TrimSpace(out) == '.git'

test_cases.description: Run returns a *GitError containing Args, ExitCode, and trimmed Stderr when the git subprocess exits with a non-zero exit code.
preconditions: A *GitRunner is constructed with a valid workDir
Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH

expected.result: ("", *GitError) where GitError.ExitCode != 0, GitError.Args contains 'cat-file', GitError.Stderr is non-empty trimmed string

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, _ := New(repoDir, nil); out, err := runner.Run(ctx, 'cat-file', '-t', 'nonexistent-sha-abc123'); assert out == ''; var ge *GitError; assert errors.As(err, &ge); assert ge.ExitCode != 0; assert len(ge.Args) > 0; assert ge.Args contains 'cat-file'

test_cases.description: Run respects context cancellation by killing the subprocess and returning the context error.
preconditions: A *GitRunner is constructed with a valid workDir
Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH

expected.result: ("", error) where error wraps context.DeadlineExceeded or context.Canceled

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1*time.Millisecond); defer cancel(); runner, _ := New(tmpDir, nil); out, err := runner.Run(ctx, 'ls-remote', 'https://localhost:1/slow'); assert out == ''; assert errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) || errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)

test_cases.description: Multiple goroutines calling Run concurrently on the same *GitRunner complete independently without data races.
preconditions: A *GitRunner is constructed with a valid git repository as workDir
Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH
Test is run with 'go test -race ./internal/gitcmd/...'

expected.results: all goroutines return valid (string, nil) results; no data race detected by -race flag

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: runner, _ := New(repoDir, nil); var wg sync.WaitGroup; results := make([]string, 20); errs := make([]error, 20); for i := 0; i < 20; i++ { wg.Add(1); go func(i int) { defer wg.Done(); results[i], errs[i] = runner.Run(ctx, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD') }(i) }; wg.Wait(); for i := 0; i < 20; i++ { assert errs[i] == nil; assert len(results[i]) == 40 }

preconditions: Host has git >= 2.38 on PATH
A valid workDir exists

property_tests.description: For any *GitRunner constructed with arbitrary extraEnv values, the subprocess environment always has the three safety variables as the last occurrences.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample extraEnv slices: nil, empty, single conflicting GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, multiple conflicting entries for all three safety vars, and a large slice with many duplicates
property_tests.invariant_check: for each sampled extraEnv: runner, _ := New(tmpDir, extraEnv); out, _ := runner.Run(ctx, 'env'); assert lastOccurrence(out, 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=') == 'GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh'; assert lastOccurrence(out, 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=') == 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0'; assert lastOccurrence(out, 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=') == 'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1'

property_tests.description: LsRemote exit code mapping is exhaustive and non-overlapping: exit 0 -> (stdout, nil), exit 2 -> ("", ErrRefNotFound), exit 1 -> ("", *GitError{ExitCode:1}).
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Three fixed scenarios: (1) local bare repo with known ref (exit 0), (2) local bare repo with absent ref (exit 2), (3) https://localhost:1/nonexistent (exit 1)
property_tests.invariant_check: scenario1: out != '' && err == nil; scenario2: out == '' && errors.Is(err, ErrRefNotFound); scenario3: out == '' && errors.As(err, &ge) && ge.ExitCode == 1; assert no scenario maps to more than one return shape

property_tests.description: Whenever Rebase returns a *RebaseConflictError, the repository's .git directory contains neither rebase-merge nor rebase-apply subdirectory.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample repositories with conflicts on different file sets (1 file, 3 files, binary file); induce conflict by creating divergent commits on feature branch and main
property_tests.invariant_check: for each conflicting repo: _, err := runner.Rebase(ctx, 'main'); var ce *RebaseConflictError; if errors.As(err, &ce) { assert !dirExists(repoDir+'/.git/rebase-merge'); assert !dirExists(repoDir+'/.git/rebase-apply') }

property_tests.description: Any number of concurrent goroutines calling any method on the same *GitRunner produce no data race as detected by the Go race detector.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Vary goroutine counts: 1, 5, 20, 50; vary methods: Run, RevParse, LsRemote (against local repo); run with 'go test -race ./internal/gitcmd/...'
property_tests.invariant_check: for each goroutine count N: launch N goroutines each calling runner.Run(ctx, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'); wait for all; assert go test -race exits 0; assert all results have len == 40

property_tests.description: If New returns a non-nil *GitRunner, the host git version is >= 2.38; if version < 2.38 or unparseable, New returns (nil, non-nil error).
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Table-driven: version strings '2.38.0', '2.39.1', '2.40.0' (expect success); '2.37.9', '2.0.0', '1.9.5' (expect error); 'malformed', '' (expect error)
property_tests.invariant_check: for each version string: major, minor, err := parseGitVersion(v); if err == nil && (major > 2 || (major == 2 && minor >= 38)) { assert constructor would succeed } else { assert constructor returns (nil, non-nil error) }

property_tests.description: Every *GitError returned by Run or any convenience method has non-empty Args, non-zero ExitCode, and Stderr equal to the trimmed stderr string.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample failing commands: invalid subcommand, invalid SHA for cat-file, invalid ref for rev-parse, invalid SHA for update-ref, unreachable remote for ls-remote
property_tests.invariant_check: for each failing command: _, err := runner.Run(ctx, args...); var ge *GitError; assert errors.As(err, &ge); assert len(ge.Args) > 0; assert ge.ExitCode != 0; assert ge.Stderr == strings.TrimSpace(ge.Stderr)

property_tests.description: MergeConflictError.ConflictingFiles has length >= 1 whenever git stdout contains at least one CONFLICT-prefixed line.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Sample conflict scenarios: single file conflict, multiple file conflicts (3 files), conflict in nested directory path; each induced in a fresh temporary repository
property_tests.invariant_check: for each conflict scenario: _, err := runner.MergeTree(ctx, base, head); var ce *MergeConflictError; assert errors.As(err, &ce); assert len(ce.ConflictingFiles) >= 1

property_tests.description: For any method call where the context is cancelled before the subprocess returns, the method returns a non-nil error wrapping the context error and does not block indefinitely.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: For each method (Run, LsRemote, MergeTree, Rebase, RebaseAbort, RevParse, UpdateRef): cancel context immediately before or during call; measure elapsed time
property_tests.invariant_check: for each method: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); cancel(); start := time.Now(); _, err := runner.Method(ctx, ...); elapsed := time.Since(start); assert err != nil; assert errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded); assert elapsed < 5*time.Second
